cell_type_model: primary astrocytes; opossum kidney proximal-tubule OK cells; murine mesangial cells
assay_or_perturbation: albumin binding and uptake assays; LRP2/megalin or Dab1/Dab2 knockdown/knockout; caveolin and clathrin perturbation
relation_type: Albumin binds LRP2/megalin and is internalized through receptor-associated endocytic machinery
pathway_branch: LRP2/megalin -> Dab1/Dab2 and caveolar or clathrin-associated endocytosis -> albumin uptake and, in astrocytes, oleate/neurotrophic output
limitations: The direct output is uptake/trafficking rather than a kinase relay; albumin handling also involves cubilin/CUBAM and cell-type-specific adaptors, and no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: COS transfectants; thymocyte/thymic epithelial adhesion models; human lymphocytes
assay_or_perturbation: ALCAM-CD6 fusion-protein binding and cell-adhesion assays; CD6-ALCAM ligation with CD3/T-cell activation and cytokine readouts
relation_type: ALCAM directly binds CD6 and ligation provides CD6-dependent costimulation of the TCR/CD3 activation program
pathway_branch: ALCAM -> CD6 costimulatory complex -> TCR/CD3-associated activation -> NF-kappaB/AP-1 and lymphocyte activation outputs
limitations: The molecular interaction is well established, but the intracellular response studies use lymphocyte costimulation rather than an SCI receiver model and do not isolate a unique CD6-only kinase cascade or terminal TF.

cell_type_model: ALCAM-CD6 adhesion systems used as receptor-family comparators
assay_or_perturbation: targeted exact-pair searches across PubMed, PMC, publisher pages, and adhesion-receptor literature; no exact ALCAM-CHL1 relay assay recovered
relation_type: No validated ALCAM-CHL1 binding or intracellular relay was recovered
pathway_branch: no exact ALCAM-CHL1 pathway established
limitations: The cited primary papers document ALCAM-CD6 binding and do not test CHL1; receptor-family, expression, neural-adhesion, or generic Ig-superfamily evidence was not transferred to this exact pair.

cell_type_model: SaOS2 osteosarcoma cells; MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts; ameloblast/periodontal cell models
assay_or_perturbation: co-immunoprecipitation and yeast-two-hybrid interaction assays; anti-CD63 blockade; Src activity and osteogenic differentiation readouts
relation_type: Ameloblastin binds CD63 and promotes a CD63-integrin-beta1 complex associated with Src inhibition and osteogenic differentiation
pathway_branch: AMBN -> CD63/integrin-beta1 membrane complex -> Src inhibition -> RhoA/ERK and osteogenic attachment/differentiation outputs
limitations: The strongest mechanistic work uses engineered or osteoblast-like systems; CD63 is a tetraspanin rather than a canonical kinase receptor, and the downstream branch is complex-level rather than a standalone CD63 pathway.

cell_type_model: ameloblast-lineage and osteoblast-like cells; multiple cultured cell lineages
assay_or_perturbation: amelogenin/CD63 binding-region mapping; co-immunoprecipitation, yeast-two-hybrid, uptake imaging, and CD63-positive vesicle localization
relation_type: Amelogenin directly interacts with CD63 and is trafficked into CD63-positive endosomal/lysosomal vesicles
pathway_branch: Amelogenin -> CD63 surface/vesicle association -> endocytic trafficking -> enamel-matrix protein clearance
limitations: The studies support binding and trafficking/clearance, not a canonical intracellular signaling relay; isoform, extracellular-fragment, and vesicle context matter, and no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: ameloblast-lineage cells; osteoblast-like and cultured epithelial/fibroblast cells
assay_or_perturbation: LAMP1/amelogenin interaction-region mapping; uptake microscopy and localization to Lamp1-positive vesicles
relation_type: Amelogenin binds LAMP1 and is internalized into Lamp1-positive vesicles
pathway_branch: Amelogenin -> LAMP1-associated endocytic trafficking -> lysosomal/enamel-matrix protein clearance
limitations: LAMP1 is a lysosomal membrane protein and the evidence supports uptake/trafficking rather than signal transduction; extracellular amelogenin isoforms and assay-specific localization limit pathway interpretation.

cell_type_model: ameloblast-lineage and cultured cell models
assay_or_perturbation: amelogenin/LAMP2 interaction-region mapping and comparison with LAMP1/CD63 binding; uptake/vesicle localization studies
relation_type: Amelogenin interacts with LAMP2 as part of enamel-matrix protein endocytic trafficking
pathway_branch: Amelogenin -> LAMP2-associated lysosomal trafficking -> enamel-matrix protein clearance
limitations: The LAMP2 evidence is primarily interaction-region and trafficking evidence, with less independent functional dissection than for LAMP1/CD63; no kinase, adaptor-specific signaling, or terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: SMAT1 cells; Müllerian-duct mesenchyme; immature granulosa cells; receptor-reconstitution and conditional-knockout mouse models
assay_or_perturbation: AMH processing and receptor activation assays; pSMAD1/5/8 immunoblotting; type-I receptor depletion and Amhr2-Cre conditional Smad/Acvr1/Bmpr1a perturbations
relation_type: Mature AMH engages AMHR2 and recruits an ACVR1-containing type-I receptor complex to activate the BMP-like SMAD1/5/8 branch
pathway_branch: AMH -> AMHR2/ACVR1 receptor complex -> SMAD1/5/8-SMAD4 -> Müllerian-duct regression and granulosa-cell response
limitations: AMH processing and type-I receptor usage are context dependent, with BMPR1A also contributing in some models; the submitted composite is a receptor-complex edge, not an isolated ACVR1 binary interaction.

cell_type_model: pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cells; EGFR-expressing heterologous cancer-cell models
assay_or_perturbation: ANG/ RNase5-EGFR association and ligand stimulation; EGFR phosphorylation, transformation, erlotinib response, and catalytic-site controls
relation_type: Angiogenin directly associates with and activates EGFR in a catalytic-independent receptor-tyrosine-kinase branch
pathway_branch: ANG -> EGFR -> receptor tyrosine phosphorylation and downstream oncogenic survival/proliferation signaling
limitations: The primary evidence is concentrated in pancreatic-cancer and heterologous cancer models; EGFR ligand potency is context dependent, and the cited studies do not establish an SCI-specific branch or terminal TF.

cell_type_model: LNCaP, PC3, DU145, glioblastoma, endothelial, neuronal, and hematopoietic stem/progenitor models; COS-7 receptor reconstitution
assay_or_perturbation: ANG binding to PLXNB2 by affinity purification, SPR, ELISA, and co-immunoprecipitation; PLXNB2 knockdown/ectopic expression; phospho-AKT/ERK, nuclear translocation, rRNA and tiRNA assays
relation_type: Angiogenin binds PLXNB2 and requires this receptor for receptor-mediated uptake/nuclear trafficking and downstream growth-survival outputs
pathway_branch: ANG -> PLXNB2 -> receptor-mediated trafficking/nuclear ANG processing -> AKT/ERK, Rac/Cdc42, rRNA/tiRNA, survival and proliferation
limitations: PLXNB2-mediated signaling is cell-type and density dependent, with ANG processing and trafficking central to the output; no single terminal TF was directly assigned.

cell_type_model: HUVECs; human and mouse brain endothelial cells; Tie2-positive and Tie2-deficient fibroblast/CHO models
assay_or_perturbation: Ang1-coated adhesion assays; alpha5beta1 blocking and expression rescue; Tie2 co-immunoprecipitation; Ang1 stimulation with FAK, p85, Akt, Tie2, migration, and survival readouts
relation_type: Ang1 directly engages alpha5beta1-dependent adhesion and cross-talks with the Tie2-alpha5beta1 complex
pathway_branch: ANGPT1 -> ITGA5/ITGB1-TIE2 complex -> FAK/p85-Akt and Tie2 signaling -> endothelial motility, survival, and angiogenic protection
limitations: Alpha5beta1 effects are matrix and Tie2-context dependent; some adhesion assays support integrin engagement without proving a single binary Ang1-ITGA5 interface, and no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: vascular endothelial cells; embryonic mouse vasculature; Tie2-transfected fibroblasts
assay_or_perturbation: Ang1/Tie2 binding and soluble-receptor competition; endothelial chemotaxis; Tie2 phosphorylation; PI3K-p85/Akt phosphorylation; survival and genetic loss-of-function assays
relation_type: Ang1 is a primary physiological ligand and agonist of the TEK/Tie2 receptor
pathway_branch: ANGPT1 -> TEK/Tie2 autophosphorylation -> PI3K-Akt and migration/survival/barrier-stabilization programs
limitations: TEK/Tie2 signaling is endothelial- and context-dependent, with multimerization and matrix presentation affecting potency; no terminal TF was directly measured.

cell_type_model: primary endothelial cells; HMEC-1; HEK293 and Tie1/Tie2 receptor-reconstitution systems
assay_or_perturbation: Ang1/Ang4 stimulation; Tie1 and Tie2 immunoprecipitation and phosphotyrosine assays; Tie2 knockdown, kinase-dead receptor, and AKT/MAPK readouts
relation_type: Ang1 induces Tie1 phosphorylation and Tie1-Tie2 signaling modulation in a Tie2-dependent receptor complex
pathway_branch: ANGPT1 -> TEK/Tie2-dependent TIE1 phosphorylation/heterodimer modulation -> AKT/MAPK and endothelial survival/morphogenesis
limitations: The primary studies do not establish a standalone Ang1-Tie1 ligand-binding event; Tie1 phosphorylation requires Tie2 and Tie1 can dampen Tie2 signaling, so this is a bounded receptor-complex relay.

cell_type_model: TIE2-low HUVECs; human glioma and breast-cancer models; endothelial spheroids and mouse angiogenesis/xenograft models
assay_or_perturbation: ANG2 adhesion and co-immunoprecipitation with alpha5beta1; integrin blocking; FAK phosphorylation, RAC1, Akt/GSK3beta, migration, invasion, and sprouting assays
relation_type: Ang2 binds and signals through alpha5beta1-containing integrin complexes, with context-dependent Tie2-independent and Tie2-cross-talk branches
pathway_branch: ANGPT2 -> ITGA5/ITGB1 (and, in some models, TIE2) -> FAK/RAC1 or ILK-Akt/GSK3beta -> migration, invasion, and sprouting
limitations: Ang2 is a context-dependent Tie2 agonist/antagonist and also binds other integrins; the composite receptor context and cancer/endothelial model determine the branch, with no terminal TF assigned.

cell_type_model: endothelial cells, including TIE2-high and TIE2-low subpopulations; mouse angiogenesis models
assay_or_perturbation: ANG2/TIE2 binding and competition with ANG1; receptor signaling, blocking-antibody, Tie2-silencing, and sprouting assays
relation_type: Ang2 engages TEK/Tie2 as a context-dependent antagonist or partial agonist of ANG1/Tie2 signaling
pathway_branch: ANGPT2 -> TEK/Tie2 -> context-dependent receptor phosphorylation or antagonism -> FAK/RAC1, endothelial migration, permeability, and sprouting
limitations: Ang2 activity depends on concentration, receptor abundance, ligand multimerization, matrix, and inflammatory context; it must not be collapsed into the constitutive Ang1/Tie2 agonist branch.

cell_type_model: primary endothelial cells and Tie1/Tie2 receptor-reconstitution systems used for angiopoietin-family comparison
assay_or_perturbation: Ang2-versus-Ang1/Ang4 Tie1 phosphorylation comparisons; Tie2-dependence and structural receptor-complex studies; no validated exact positive Ang2-Tie1 activation branch recovered
relation_type: No validated direct Ang2-Tie1 activation or Ang2-specific Tie1 relay was recovered
pathway_branch: no exact Ang2 -> Tie1 branch established
limitations: Native Ang1 and Ang4, but not native Ang2, induced Tie1 phosphorylation in the key primary comparison; Ang2-Tie2 antagonism/partial agonism and generic Tie1/Tie2 family evidence were not transferred to this exact pair.

cell_type_model: blood and lymphatic endothelial cells; peripheral-retina endothelial models
assay_or_perturbation: Ang4 stimulation; Tie2, Akt, and ERK phosphorylation immunoblotting; permeability, lymphatic dilation, venous maturation, and Tie2 perturbation assays
relation_type: Ang4 activates the TEK/Tie2 receptor branch and produces endothelial and lymphatic functional outputs
pathway_branch: ANGPT4 -> TEK/Tie2 -> PI3K-Akt and ERK -> endothelial permeability, lymphatic dilation, and venous maturation
limitations: Ang4 processing, species, tissue, and vascular-bed context affect signaling; the primary studies emphasize functional receptor activation rather than a purified full-length binding structure, and no terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: primary endothelial cells and HMEC-1 angiopoietin-receptor assays
assay_or_perturbation: native Ang4 stimulation with Tie1/Tie2 immunoprecipitation and phosphotyrosine measurements
relation_type: Native Ang4 induces Tie1 phosphorylation in a Tie2-associated angiopoietin receptor context
pathway_branch: ANGPT4 -> TIE1/TIE2-associated receptor complex -> Tie1 phosphorylation and vascular morphogenesis modulation
limitations: The primary evidence supports Tie1 phosphorylation but does not resolve a standalone Ang4-Tie1 ligand-binding interface or a distinct downstream branch; Tie2 co-receptor dependence and angiopoietin multimerization remain limitations.

cell_type_model: CL1-5 human lung adenocarcinoma cells; HCC and endothelial comparator models
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant ANGPTL1 binding to alpha1beta1 by ELISA/SPR and co-immunoprecipitation; integrin knockdown/blockade; FAK/ERK/Akt, miR-630, SP1/SLUG, motility, and angiogenesis assays
relation_type: ANGPTL1 engages alpha1beta1 and suppresses motility/angiogenic outputs through integrin-associated FAK/ERK signaling
pathway_branch: ANGPTL1 -> ITGA1/ITGB1 -> FAK/ERK/Akt and SP1-miR-630/SLUG regulatory branch -> reduced migration, invasion, and angiogenesis
limitations: The primary mechanistic evidence is cancer-cell and endothelial-context dependent and reports an inhibitory rather than agonist-like branch; related ANGPTL1 literature includes a retracted later paper, which was excluded from this record.

cell_type_model: ATDC5 chondrocytes; murine macrophages and peritoneal cells; human gingival epithelial cells
assay_or_perturbation: ANGPTL2 stimulation; alpha5beta1 blocking antibody or integrin perturbation; MAPK, Akt, NF-kappaB phosphorylation, inflammatory-gene, adhesion, and cytokine readouts
relation_type: ANGPTL2 activates an alpha5beta1-associated inflammatory relay, with receptor-blocking evidence but context-dependent direct-binding resolution
pathway_branch: ANGPTL2 -> ITGA5/ITGB1 -> ERK/JNK/p38-Akt-NF-kappaB -> inflammatory cytokine and matrix-remodeling outputs
limitations: These studies support receptor-dependent signaling and in some models adhesion, but do not uniformly provide purified binary binding; PIRB is an alternative ANGPTL2 receptor in hematopoietic contexts and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: mouse and human hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells; PirB/LILRB2-transfected 293T and reporter cells; leukemia models
assay_or_perturbation: ANGPTL2/PIRB binding and receptor phosphorylation; SHP-1/SHP-2 recruitment; CAMKIV phosphorylation; PirB/LILRB2 gain/loss, reporter, and stem-cell expansion assays
relation_type: ANGPTL2 binds PIRB/LILRB2 and activates an ITIM-associated receptor relay supporting hematopoietic stem/progenitor-cell outputs
pathway_branch: ANGPTL2 -> PIRB/LILRB2 ITIM phosphorylation -> SHP1/SHP2 -> CAMKIV and stem-cell self-renewal/expansion programs
limitations: Mouse PIRB and human LILRB2 are orthologous but not identical; ANGPTL family members can share this receptor, and the strongest functional studies are hematopoietic rather than SCI-specific. No terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: HUVECs; diabetic mouse retina and retinal vascular models
assay_or_perturbation: ANGPTL3 overexpression/knockout and evinacumab perturbation; alpha5 co-immunoprecipitation/knockdown; endothelial barrier, junctional ZO-1/VE-cadherin, and leakage assays
relation_type: ANGPTL3 directly associates with integrin alpha5 and drives an alpha5-dependent endothelial barrier/permeability branch
pathway_branch: ANGPTL3 -> ITGA5-containing integrin complex -> endothelial junction remodeling -> vascular leakage
limitations: The study resolves an alpha5 interaction but does not fully define the beta-chain partner or a canonical kinase relay; it is a recent retinal-disease model and does not establish an SCI-specific receiver context.

cell_type_model: HUVECs and rat corneal angiogenesis model; recombinant-protein systems
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant ANGPTL3 binding to alphaVbeta3; integrin-blocking and haptotactic adhesion/migration assays; Akt, MAPK, and FAK phosphorylation; in vivo corneal angiogenesis
relation_type: ANGPTL3 directly binds alphaVbeta3 and activates integrin-dependent endothelial migration and angiogenic signaling
pathway_branch: ANGPTL3 -> ITGAV/ITGB3 -> FAK-Akt-MAPK -> endothelial adhesion, migration, and angiogenesis
limitations: The study uses recombinant ANGPTL3 and endothelial/corneal models and does not establish a terminal TF or SCI-specific context; ANGPTL3 did not bind TEK/Tie2 in the same receptor-comparison experiments.

cell_type_model: fibroblast and scar-remodeling models; recombinant C-terminal ANGPTL4/CDH11 complex systems
assay_or_perturbation: cANGPTL4-CDH11 binding and complex assays; ANGPTL4 fragment perturbation; beta-catenin-mediated ID3 expression, collagen, and wound-healing readouts
relation_type: C-terminal ANGPTL4 binds CDH11 and modulates a cadherin-catenin complex associated with fibroblast scar-remodeling output
pathway_branch: cANGPTL4 -> CDH11/CTNND1/CTNNB1 complex -> beta-catenin-dependent ID3 regulation -> reduced scar-collagen output
limitations: The interaction is fragment- and cadherin-complex dependent; the primary study is fibroblast/scar context rather than SCI, and beta-catenin is a transcriptional coactivator endpoint rather than evidence of a direct ANGPTL4-TF interaction.

cell_type_model: endothelial cells; tumor-cell/endothelial co-culture and metastasis models
assay_or_perturbation: cANGPTL4-CDH5/VE-cadherin direct-interaction assays; endothelial junction imaging; ANGPTL4 knockout/knockdown and vascular-permeability perturbations
relation_type: C-terminal ANGPTL4 binds VE-cadherin/CDH5 in a sequential junctional complex; the associated phenotype is junction declustering rather than a standalone CDH5 relay
pathway_branch: cANGPTL4 -> CDH5/VE-cadherin junction complex, with parallel ITGA5/ITGB1-Rac1/PAK signaling -> endothelial-junction disruption and permeability
limitations: The primary study assigns Rac1/PAK activation to the parallel alpha5beta1 branch and CDH5 to sequential complex declustering; it does not establish a CDH5-proximal kinase cascade or terminal TF.
